lessons.title: A comparison with no winner
lessons.why: A comparison is a set of sentences you can point at. A ranking is a sentence these pages do not contain.
depends: The pages listed on this track
body: Each later room uses a page this lab opened in October 2026. The product name is the name printed on that page. If two pages use two names, both names stay, with the page each one came from. Bars in this track are equal on purpose. Length is not a rank, a price, or a market share.

Words such as a superlative for quality, a prize, or a promise of no effort are not used here, even when a vendor page uses them. The Teams contact-center article links a certified-solutions list. This track does not paste that list, and it does not paste a different app index.

lessons.fault: A slide declares a winner using a word that is not on the opened page.
lessons.listen: This comparison cites opened pages only. It does not rank vendors and it does not invent prices.

lessons.title: What the Microsoft pages name
lessons.why: Microsoft publishes more than one voice path. The page you cite has to be the path you mean.
body: The Dynamics voice-channel page says the channel provides native PSTN calling in Dynamics 365, is built on Azure Communication Services, and routes calls with unified routing. The Teams Phone page says a Teams number used with Contact Center is a Calling Plan service number, Operator Connect, or Direct Routing, and that the representative is notified in Copilot Service workspace.

The Teams contact-center article names three models for a provider: Unify, using Azure Communication Services call automation and the calling SDK. Extend, where the Teams client is the calling endpoint and the provider acts as a telephony carrier alongside Microsoft 365. Connect, using a certified SBC and Direct Routing. A note on Connect says the contact-center agent does not need a phone-system license, and the Teams user does, plus a number, for transfer. The article links a certified list. This room does not copy vendor names from a different index.

flow.label: Teams number
flow.detail: Service number, Operator Connect, or Direct Routing

lessons.say: I can say which Microsoft article I am quoting before I name a model.
lessons.fault: Extend, which uses the Teams client, is described with the Dynamics workspace notification.
lessons.listen: Quote the Dynamics voice channel, the Teams number bridge, or the three provider models. They are different pages.

lessons.title: Amazon Connect Customer
lessons.why: The admin guide opened for this room uses a current product name that is not the old title.
depends: The Amazon Connect Customer page in the sources
body: That guide says Amazon Connect Customer is the current name for the product previously called Amazon Connect. It says Amazon Connect is now a set of agentic AI solutions for different business functions, and that this guide covers Amazon Connect Customer. This room uses that distinction and does not describe the other functions.

The page says agents spend time on voice, chat, SMS, or other channels. It says administrators provision phone numbers, and with managers they define queues, routing profiles, and flows. It says you pay only for what you use, and it links a pricing page. This room does not copy a price. Salesforce’s pages, in the previous track, name Amazon Connect as one telephony path into Partner Contact Center. That is a Salesforce sentence, not an Amazon ranking.

lessons.title: CCAI Platform and the GECX rename
lessons.why: The docs page and the legal change log do not print the same product title. Both were opened.
body: The docs page opened for this room is titled Contact Center AI Platform. It says CCAI Platform is built natively on Google Cloud, uses other Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience products, and is purpose-built to work alongside CRMs. It says the platform queues and routes voice and digital channels, names Virtual Agent, Agent Assist, and Insights, and says it reports on agent performance and customer satisfaction. It links a locations page. This room does not copy the country list.

The legal change log contains this line: Updated name of Customer Engagement Suite and Contact Center AI to Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience (GECX). A different line says the service terms for Contact Center AI Platform were renamed to Google Cloud Contact Center as a Service in a section of those terms, and another line says the services-summary name for CCAI Platform was updated toward Google Cloud Contact Center as a Service. The docs page opened here still uses Contact Center AI Platform. This room does not say that docs page was renamed away.

chart.title: Two Google pages

lessons.say: The docs page still says Contact Center AI Platform. The change log records the GECX rename.

lessons.title: Documented differences only
lessons.why: A table is safe when every cell comes from a page you can reopen.
depends: The four product rooms in this track
body: Dynamics, on the voice-channel page: native PSTN calling in Dynamics, built on Azure Communication Services, routed with unified routing, with customer and case lookup in the capabilities table. Teams providers, on the contact-center page: Unify, Extend, or Connect, as the previous room states. Amazon Connect Customer, on its guide: agents on voice, chat, SMS, or other channels, and administrators on numbers, queues, routing profiles, and flows. CCAI Platform, on its docs page: queuing and routing across voice and digital, working alongside CRMs, and using other Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience products. Salesforce, on the help page: Partner Contact Center, with Amazon Connect and partner-telephony models still named.
Read down a column only. Do not add a column for a score. The chart on this page uses the same length for each page so a longer bar cannot be mistaken for a preference.

lessons.title: What these pages do not decide
lessons.why: The honest end of a comparison is the list of questions the opened pages do not answer.
body: These pages do not state a price figure this room can repeat. Amazon’s guide says you pay only for what you use and links pricing. No amount is copied. They do not state market share. They do not rank the products. The Teams article links a certified-solutions list and a list of providers in the certification process. This track does not paste either list.

A country list, a license SKU, and an edition matrix stay on the page that owns them. Track 14 remains the place for coexistence designs this campus already wrote. If a newer page disagrees with this room, the newer page wins. The access month is October 2026.
lessons.say: I can say what this comparison refuses to decide.
lessons.fault: A missing cell is filled with a remembered price or a rank.
lessons.listen: These pages do not decide price numbers, market share, or a winner. A certified list stays on Microsoft’s page.
